From the grep results, I see imports like `from "../../../elements/ui"` — so they use relative paths. In the coda desktop, from `coda/desktop/` to `elements/ui/` the relative path would be `../../elements/ui`.

Now let me plan the refactoring:


The elements/ui components have different APIs than what coda desktop uses — the Button component uses ButtonGroup internally with different variant options, the Card doesn't support an action prop, and I need to check what the Spinner looks like too.

Looking at the other available components, there's Collapsible built on Radix, Tabs, Tree structures, Accordion, and Layout components that handle navbar, footer, and canvas areas. The Navbar and Footer have their own prop structures, and I'll need to wrap everything with LevelProvider for theming.

The main challenge is that these elements components work differently from what I'm used to—they're more primitive and composable, the Button doesn't have loading or variant states, and everything relies on the Level context. So I need to add the dependency, set up the Vite alias, swap out my custom components for these, wrap the app with LevelProvider, and update the global styles to pull in the right theme.

Looking at the Button component specifically, it supports variants like default, ghost, and outline through ButtonGroupItem, but there's no built-in loading state or disabled variant—I'll need to handle those through custom styling or by passing disabled as a prop that flows through naturally.

The real challenge is that the refactoring task asks to use only elements/ui, but the coda desktop has domain-specific components like StatusBadge, OntologyTree, and ValidationTree that don't exist in that library. I think the intent is to swap out the generic reusable components (Button, Card, Spinner, Input) with elements/ui equivalents, while keeping the specialized components but rebuilding them to use elements/ui as their foundation.
